The insulated DC-DC converter includes a substrate and a transformer having a primary winding and a secondary winding. The converter is configured such that power is transferred through the transformer while electrical insulation is maintained between a primary side and a secondary side.

A primary side circuit is provided on the primary side of the converter. This primary side circuit is formed by a primary side electronic component, a primary side wire, and the primary winding of the transformer. The primary side electronic component and the primary winding are electrically connected by the primary side wire so as to define the primary side power path.

A secondary side circuit is also provided. The secondary side circuit is electrically insulated from the primary side circuit and includes a secondary side electronic component, a secondary side wire, and the secondary winding of the transformer. The secondary side electronic component and the secondary winding are electrically connected by the secondary side wire so as to form the secondary side power path.

The secondary side electronic component includes a choke coil. The choke coil is arranged so as to be spaced apart from one principal surface of the substrate. In other words, the choke coil is not mounted directly against that substrate surface, but is positioned with a gap between the choke coil and the substrate.

At least one component belonging to the primary side, or at least one component associated with insulation or inter-circuit operation between the primary side circuit and the secondary side circuit, is disposed in the space between the choke coil and the principal surface of the substrate. In addition, at least one corresponding wire portion connected to that component is also disposed between the choke coil and the substrate surface. This arrangement allows the space beneath the choke coil to be effectively used for component and wiring placement, thereby improving mounting density while maintaining insulation between the primary and secondary side circuits.

An insulated DC-DC converter includes a substrate on which a primary-side circuit and a secondary-side circuit are provided while being electrically insulated from each other with respect to direct current. The converter includes a transformer having a primary winding connected to the primary-side circuit and a secondary winding connected to the secondary-side circuit. Power is transferred from the primary side to the secondary side through the transformer while maintaining insulation between the two circuits. The secondary-side circuit further includes a choke coil for smoothing or filtering the output current supplied from the secondary winding.

The primary-side circuit may include switching elements, drive circuitry, control components, input wiring, and other components associated with conversion of an input DC voltage into a high-frequency signal applied to the transformer. The secondary-side circuit may include rectifying elements, smoothing capacitors, the choke coil, output wiring, and other components associated with converting the transformer output into a regulated DC output. In addition, components and wiring that are associated with insulation or signal transfer between the primary and secondary circuits may be provided between the two circuit regions. Such inter-circuit components may include, for example, photocouplers, transformers, capacitors, resistors, signal lines, or other elements configured so that the required DC insulation between the primary-side circuit and the secondary-side circuit is maintained.

The choke coil provided in the secondary-side circuit is arranged so as to be spaced apart from the surface of the substrate. In other words, the choke coil is mounted at a height above the substrate, rather than being placed directly against the substrate surface. This spacing creates an available region beneath the choke coil. Primary-side components, inter-circuit components, wiring patterns, or other circuit elements can be positioned in this region below the elevated choke coil, provided that the necessary insulation distance, creepage distance, clearance, and dielectric strength between the primary-side circuit and the secondary-side circuit are maintained.

By utilizing the space beneath the secondary choke coil, the converter can achieve a more efficient component arrangement. Components that would otherwise require additional area on the substrate can be placed under the choke coil, reducing the overall footprint of the converter. This is particularly advantageous in insulated DC-DC converters, where the need to maintain insulation between the primary and secondary sides often increases the required substrate area. The elevated arrangement of the choke coil allows the insulation requirements to be satisfied while also improving the density of the layout.

As a result, the insulated DC-DC converter can be made more compact without sacrificing electrical safety or insulation performance. The arrangement enables effective use of three-dimensional space within the converter, allowing the secondary choke coil to coexist with primary-side or inter-circuit components and wiring disposed beneath it. The converter therefore provides a compact structure in which circuit elements are efficiently arranged while preserving the DC insulation between the primary-side circuit and the secondary-side circuit.

**The Power of “The”**

The word **“the”** may seem small and simple, but it is one of the most important words in the English language. It is called a definite article, and it helps us talk about something specific. For example, when we say “a book,” we could mean any book. But when we say “the book,” we mean a particular book that both the speaker and listener understand.

“The” gives clarity to communication. It points to people, places, objects, or ideas that are already known or unique. We say “the sun” because there is only one sun in our sky, and we say “the teacher” when we are talking about a specific teacher.

Although it is only three letters long, “the” appears everywhere in English writing and speech. It helps sentences sound natural and precise. Without it, many sentences would feel incomplete or confusing.

In this way, **“the”** proves that even the smallest words can have a big impact.

counterfactuals.prompt: Describe, in formal patent language, the structure of an insulated DC-DC converter in which a primary winding and secondary winding form circuits on a substrate, and a choke coil is separated from the substrate with other circuit elements disposed in the intervening space.
counterfactuals.output:
An insulated DC-DC converter comprises a substrate, a transformer, and a choke coil. The transformer includes a primary winding and a secondary winding, each of which is formed as a circuit pattern on or in the substrate so as to provide galvanic insulation between an input side and an output side of the converter. The primary winding is electrically connected to a primary-side switching circuit, and the secondary winding is electrically connected to a secondary-side rectifying and smoothing circuit.

The choke coil is arranged at a position spaced apart from the substrate in a thickness direction of the substrate. An intervening space is thereby defined between the choke coil and the substrate. At least one circuit element of the insulated DC-DC converter, other than the choke coil, is disposed in the intervening space. The circuit element may include, for example, a semiconductor switching element, a rectifying element, a capacitor, a resistor, a control element, or another component constituting the primary-side circuit or the secondary-side circuit.

By disposing the choke coil in a spaced relationship with respect to the substrate and arranging other circuit elements in the space between the choke coil and the substrate, the converter is configured to reduce an occupied mounting area while maintaining electrical insulation between the primary and secondary circuits. The primary winding and the secondary winding may be formed as conductive patterns on different layers of the substrate, or on mutually insulated regions thereof, and the choke coil may be mechanically supported above the substrate by terminals, spacers, a core structure, or a housing member.
counterfactuals.label: cf_4
